items.claim: tier-burn-deny.py denies at N consecutive execution calls since the operator's last message (default 40 Opus / 12 Fable, env-overridable), stopping the count at the first human message or the first delegation call, and separately denies a 4th Fable call in one arc unless the human text says 'fable ok'; Grep/Glob and pure delegation calls are never counted as execution.

image-open-ask.py asks before the 8th raw image in a chat (denies instead under permission_mode bypassPermissions), covers Read of an image file, any mcp__ tool whose name contains 'screenshot', and mcp__*__computer with action screenshot/zoom, and stays silent on 'images ok' or an executor session.

context-size-warn.py prints CONTEXT <n>K once per 50K band once a chat's last recorded usage is at or over 200K tokens, tracked per session_id in <HARNESS_STATE_DIR>/context-warn.json, and stays silent under 200K, on a repeat in the same band, with no usage recorded, or for an executor session.

All three hooks are wired into .claude/settings.json in the exact order and shape C.4 specifies (two new PreToolUse entries appended after the existing three, one new UserPromptSubmit key), and the file still parses as JSON.

Every changed path in the working tree at verification time was on this brief's own Files list (the 3 new hooks, the 3 new tests and settings.json; this digest is the Files list's 8th and last entry, written after verification ran).

deviations: The brief's C.5 header says every hook call in this run gets a fresh temp HARNESS_STATE_DIR, but C2 cases 1, 2 and 4 all name session s1 and case 2 is explicitly 'again' at a higher token count expecting 'nothing', which only tests anything if the persisted band survives between calls. test_c2_context_warn.py shares one HARNESS_STATE_DIR across cases 1, 2 and 4 (each still gets its own fresh transcript file); cases 3, 5 and 6 each get an independent fresh state dir. Same reading test_b2_governor.py's own docstring gave the identical tension in run B.

Definitions implemented exactly as written are not exercised by the given 15-case B3 table: the mcp__ EXEC substrings (claude_browser, chrome, playwright, computer-use), the Skill and AskUserQuestion delegation names, and the HARNESS_TIER_BURN_FABLE env override (only HARNESS_TIER_BURN_OPUS is exercised, case 15) never fire, since all 15 cases use only Bash, Edit, Grep and Agent. Self-certified pending confirmation against a real transcript.

Neither brief names the literal JSON key a live PreToolUse payload uses for the current call's own id. tier-burn-deny.py reads payload.get('tool_use_id') and the test fixtures set that same key to a value that never collides with the transcript ('current0001'), so the id-skip branch in both the Fable-count and the consecutive-execution walk is a defensive no-op in every case by construction (the current call is never already in its own transcript tail). If the real payload carries a different key, or none, behavior is unchanged.
